description: All your computers and your phone, working as one desk. Screens, apps, files, clipboard, calls, texts, notifications, mouse and keyboard, shared between Mac, Windows, Linux and Android. Free and open source. No account, no cloud, and now no shared network needed.

latest_release.name: TwinDesk v2.5.3 :  ReZume, an all-new look, and a new engine underneath
latest_release.body:
## 🩹 v2.5.1 - v2.5.3: hot patch on v2.5.0

- **Big single files stopped at about 5 minutes** ([#143](https://github.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/issues/143)).  Phone and pc keep awake while transferring
- **Linux: mouse sharing on older distros** ([#149](https://github.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/issues/149)
- **Files bigger than 4 GiB** ([#143](https://github.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/issues/143)). A single file over 4 GiB didn't start. That limit is gone, on every computer and the phone. Both sides need 2.5.2.
- **Faster files with the phone** ([#143](https://github.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/issues/143)). The phone sent and received file bytes as base64 text, a third more data than the file itself. It now uses the direct HTTPS stream the computers use. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct work as before.
- **New: Files › Encrypt file transfers** (on by default). Turn it off on both computers, or on the computer a phone is paired with, and file bytes go over the local network without encryption. Everything else stays encrypted, and every file is still checked, so a change on the way is caught. Over a USB cable the phone always encrypts.
- **Linux: input access is TwinDesk's helper's alone** ([#144](https://github.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/issues/144)). 
- **General was blank in Multi-device mode** ([#142](https://github.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/issues/142)). With Multi-device (the MESH beta) on, the General page drew its heading and nothing else, on Mac, Windows and Linux. It works again
- **Known: ReZume is one-to-one only for now.** Multi-device mode doesn't have ReZume yet, and the phone says "ReZume isn't available on …" while the computer is in it. To use ReZume, go to Multi-device and choose Turn off: TwinDesk restarts in one-to-one mode, where the ReZume tab is.


Update every computer and phone you pair to 2.5.3. The in-app updater offers it.

---

## TwinDesk 2.5: ReZume, an all-new look, and a new engine underneath

https://twin-desk.vercel.app

![TwinDesk 2.5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/main/.github/assets/v25-banner.jpg)

The biggest TwinDesk release so far. **ReZume** carries what you were doing to the other screen. Every app has **a new look**, in light and dark. Under it, the mouse and keyboard run on **tdv2**, a new UDP protocol written in Rust, and files move on **fx2**, a new transfer engine.

detail.readme_excerpt:
TwinDesk

Your Mac, your PC, your Linux box and your Android phone, working as one desk.
One mouse and keyboard for all of them. Their screens, apps, files, clipboard, cameras, calls and texts, shared.
Free and open source. No account, no cloud, no shared network needed.

⬇️ Download 2.5 · Website · What's new · What it does · Get started

## What is TwinDesk? You probably own more than one computer. A work laptop and a gaming PC. A MacBook and the Windows machine you can't give up. A Linux box under the desk. And a phone that's never more than a metre away. Each one is great on its own. Together they're a mess: two keyboards, files emailed to yourself, a phone you keep picking up, the same tab opened three times. **TwinDesk turns all of them into one desk.** Push the mouse off the edge of your Mac's screen and it carries on onto the PC, keyboard and all. Copy on one, paste on the other. Drag a file across the edge and drop it there. Open the PC's apps in windows on your Mac. Turn a tablet or an old laptop into a second screen. Answer your phone's calls and texts from the computer, use its camera in your video calls, and drive the computer from the couch with it. And when you walk from one device to another, **ReZume** brings the tab, the video or the document you were on with you. It's one app on every platform, so a Mac and a PC pair exactly like two Macs, and a phone is a full peer instead of a notification mirror.
**🔀 Any combination**
Mac ↔ Windows, Mac ↔ Mac, PC ↔ PC, Linux ↔ anything, Android ↔ any computer. Or [all of them at once](#me
